# Sebago (05, engineer) — BAD-078

## Brief
One change, on branch `feat/bad-078-movecheck`: give `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s test job the git history `npm test` now needs.

## Why

BAD-078 adds `test/movecheck.test.js`, which reads the pre-split side of six historical splits out of git with `git show 5751929^:web/app.js`. `actions/checkout@v7` clones shallow by default, so on a runner those revisions do not exist and every corpus test dies with `fatal: invalid object name`.

That already turned `ci.yml`'s `test` and `test-windows` jobs red on this PR; BADS-078/Katahdin fixed those. She then found that **`release.yml` has the same shape and nobody has tripped it yet**: line 38 checks out with the action's defaults, line 47 runs `npm test`. Left alone, this PR lands a landmine that fires on the next tag release rather than on any PR — the worst place to find it.

## The change

Add `fetch-depth: 0` to the checkout at `.github/workflows/release.yml:38`, with a short comment saying why, exactly as Katahdin did in `ci.yml`. **Read her `ci.yml` diff first (`git show HEAD -- .github/workflows/ci.yml`, or just read the file) and match it** — spelling, comment register and placement. The `changes` job in `ci.yml` is the older precedent for the same line. History here is 840 commits, 20 MiB packed, so a full fetch is cheap; that is why this is the fix and not something cleverer.

Then check the rest of that file and every other workflow: `grep -rn 'npm test\|npm run test' .github/workflows/` finds every job with this dependency. `ci.yml:124`, `ci.yml:252` and `release.yml:47` are the three known. **Confirm each one's checkout either already has the depth or gets it, and confirm you have not missed a workflow.** Change nothing that does not run `npm test`.

## Done when

- Every job in `.github/workflows/` that runs `npm test` checks out with full history, and you list them in your Result with the line numbers you checked.
- `release.yml` parses — `gh workflow view release.yml` or any YAML parse — and the diff is two lines plus a comment.
- You state what you did **not** change and why, so the next reader knows the sweep was deliberate rather than partial.

You cannot run CI or a release; Spud pushes and reads the run. No test to run for this one — say so rather than inventing one.
